units.evidence: [Wikipedia: Hurricane Patricia] "Patricia reached hurricane strength shortly after 00:00 UTC on October 22" ... "The hurricane reached its peak intensity at around 12:00 UTC on October 23"; "Patricia's one-minute maximum sustained winds ranked as the highest ever reliably observed or estimated in a tropical cyclone"; "Within 24 hours of moving ashore, Patricia weakened into a tropical depression and dissipated soon thereafter"; "dissipated on October 24 over central Mexico, less than 18 hours after moving ashore"
units.note: All quotes are verbatim. Last moment as a tropical storm (just before 00:00 UTC 22 October) to peak (about 12:00 UTC 23 October) is about 36 hours, so 'about a day and a half' holds on the pinned meteorological history. The cited 'growth' and 'peak' quotes alone do not show the 36 hours; the meteorological history in the same pinned article does. 'In a tropical cyclone' is restored. 'Faded within a day of landfall' fits both the 24-hour and the under-18-hours wording. 'Measured' for 'observed' is fine. Dropping 'one-minute' does not change the truth here: no tropical cyclone has a higher wind on any averaging period.

units.evidence: [Wikipedia: Alberto Santos-Dumont] "These were the first heavier-than-air flights certified by the Aeroclub of France, the first such flights officially witnessed by an aeronautics recordkeeping body"; [Wikipedia: Biplane] "The first powered, controlled aeroplane to fly, the Wright Flyer"
units.note: The first sentence is supported. In the second, 'one' can only refer back to 'powered, controlled aeroplane', so it says a record body certified an aeroplane. The source says the Aero-Club certified flights, not a machine, and 'certified aeroplane' sounds like airworthiness certification. It also quietly makes the 14-bis a 'controlled' aeroplane. The pinned article gives Santos-Dumont's own account of 23 October ('after sixty meters, I lost direction and crashed'), and says he added rudimentary ailerons before 12 November. The takeaway already uses the right noun ('the first aeroplane flight that an official body certified'). The spoken line matches the caption, with the name respelled. Minor: the Wright sentence sits on the 14-bis photo (m3). It works only because frames 1 to 3 already showed that image as the 14-bis.
units.fix: Second sentence: "Santos-Dumont made the first aeroplane flight that a record body certified." Change the say line the same way ("Santos-Doomon made the first aeroplane flight that a record body certified.").
units.resolved: Now "Santos-Dumont made the first aeroplane flight that a record body certified." The spoken line matches.

units.evidence: Commons API extmetadata for the file: Artist "James St. John" (Flickr jsjgeology), DateTimeOriginal "2010-06-11 11:40", LicenseShortName "CC BY 2.0", AttributionRequired "true", 2859×2000; description: "(cast, FMNH PF15316 & PF15318, Field Museum...)" and "The specimen seen here consists of a skull and post-cranial skeleton."
units.note: The credit misattributes. 'James St' cuts the photographer's surname: he is James St. John. This is a CC BY 2.0 image, so attribution is required. The licence, the year 2010 and the size match Commons. Alt text: I viewed the 1280px file. It shows a cast of a long, flat, wedge-shaped skull with an eye socket, then dark reddish-brown body and shoulder pieces on the right, on a pale grey wall. 'Cast', 'flat head' and 'start of the body behind it' are right. But the bone is tan and buff with brown patches, not grey: grey is the background.
units.fix: credit: "James St John, 2010, cropped" (no full stop after St, so nothing splits). alt: "Cast of a Tiktaalik fossil skull: a long, flat head of tan and brown bone, with the start of the body behind it".
units.resolved: Credit now "James St John, 2010" (", cropped" is added because the frame crops a CC BY file). Alt now says "tan and brown bone".
